profile.headline: Software Engineer
profile.summary: I'm currently a student at Johns Hopkins University pursuing the combined MSE and BS degrees in Computer Science as well as an undergraduate double major in Applied Mathematics and Statistics.  Additionally, I am a student athlete on the track and cross country teams. I am particularly interested in cybersecurity and low-level programming. I have programming experience in C, Java, Assembly and various other languages.

positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.description: Collaborated with a team to design, implement and test a client-facing dynamic specification generator program. Individually created an internal tool to query product protocol information from the codebase. Identified and patched pre-existing bugs, and product limitations.

positions.title: Teaching Assistant
positions.description:
Worked as a TA for Discrete Mathematics Fall 2020 and Spring 2021 semesters within the Applied Math department at Johns Hopkins University. Taught a weekly section, reviewing course topics and practice problems from the previous assignments. Graded student homework assignments. Organized Piazza board, an online platform where students can easily ask questions of professors and teaching assistants.
Worked as a TA for a two-week January term Introductory R course within the Applied Math department at Johns Hopkins University. Led breakout room class sessions, reviewing course topics and practice problems as well as weekly office hours. Graded student homework assignments.

positions.title: Student Trainee in Mathematics
positions.description:
Worked as part of the Identity and Access Management team to improve and trouble shoot the
manual proofing process. Researched best practices in IAM and presented findings to team to make actionable change to current processes. Researched and completed an oral presentation to Information Systems Group on the potential of introducing Machine Learning techniques into the current IT procedures. Identified a security risk in current processes and presented to various managers and security leads on the requirements, problem, and proposed solution.

positions.title: NSF REU Research Intern
positions.description:
Conducted research on Simplelink Wireless Technology. Worked with another student and an
advising professor to design a protocol for and implement an over the update for wireless sensor
networks. The project involved knowledge of telecommunications engineering, encryption and
authentication protocols, and IoT networks, as well as, requiring C programming and software engineering skills. Wrote a final research paper and prepared an oral presentation on the results. The paper was accepted into the 2019 REUNS conference in Monterey, California.

educations.fieldOfStudy: Computer Science, Applied Mathematics and Statistics
